notes: Quick summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Evaluating Hosted API first; moving toward Dedicated for predictable latency & data isolation.
Use patterns: mix of short in-app prompts (autocomplete/help) and longer chat/history for guided product walkthroughs; embeddings for doc-search and reranking on product docs.
Hosted trial (14 days): ~1.0M tokens consumed in trial window; team ran integration with 3 routes (chat, embeddings, rerank).
POC key metrics (trial extrapolated): p95 latency (short prompts) ~230ms on hosted, p95 latency (long chat w/history) ~850ms; embeddings avg latency ~120ms.
Observed behavior: KV cache hit ~18% on chat history; larger long-chat requests drive token cost spike. Need improved caching + prefix trimming.
Traffic profile (extrapolated): avg QPS ~45, peak QPS ~150 during product release spikes; expected concurrency 40-80 streams with burst patterns at 10-15 minute intervals.
Token mix (trial -> forecast): short_prompts: 60% (<=50 tokens), long_chat: 30% (500-2000 tokens depending on context), embeddings: 10% (avg 256 tokens).

Dedicated sizing recommendation from SE: 2 x A100-equivalent nodes for baseline steady-state, +1 burst pool node to cover peak QPS; configure batching window 25-40ms and enable KV prefix caching to reduce tokens.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market procurement focused on predictable monthly commit; interested in reserved capacity pricing with auto-burst and clear unit economics.
Security: require SOC2 attestation, SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, audit logs and option for EU data residency for some customers.

Quotes from stakeholders: 'Need predictable latency during our weekly release windows — can't have 2x latency spikes.' - Head of Product; 'Pricing needs to be committed or we risk 3rd-party infra variance' - Finance.
Next gate: finalize Dedicated sizing and sign MSA + SOW; legal review on residency + retention clauses is the last blocker.
